ai.literal: Unfailing harvests and worthy people, decline-without wealthy people and, that which gathers is a country.
ai.translation: A true country is one that gathers unfailing harvests, worthy people, and wealthy people whose fortunes do not decline.
ai.modern: குறையாத விளைச்சலும், தகுதியுடைய சான்றோரும், தாழ்வில்லாத செல்வரும் ஒருங்கே சேர்ந்திருப்பதே சிறந்த நாடாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet defines the essential components of a prosperous country. It lists three vital elements: unfailing agricultural yields, virtuous and capable citizens, and wealthy individuals whose riches do not diminish. The word 'சேர்வது' emphasizes that a true nation is formed by the harmonious gathering of these three resources. Together, they ensure economic stability, moral integrity, and continuous prosperity for the land.

ai.literal: With great wealth having become a desired thing, by rare ruin abundantly that which yields is a country.
ai.translation: A true country is one that is desired for its great wealth, and which yields abundantly while remaining free from ruin.
ai.modern: மிகுந்த செல்வத்தால் அனைவராலும் விரும்பப்படுவதாகி, கேடுகள் இல்லாததாய், மிகுதியாக விளைச்சலைத் தருவதே சிறந்த நாடாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet defines the ideal characteristics of a prosperous country. It must possess great wealth, making it a desirable place for people to live and thrive. Furthermore, it must be free from destructive forces, indicated by the word 'அருங்கேடு' (rare ruin), and consistently produce abundant yields to sustain its population.

ai.literal: Burden together upon when coming having borne, to the king tax fully that which pays is a country.
ai.translation: A true country is one that can bear a heavy burden when it falls upon it all at once, and still pay its taxes in full to the king.
ai.modern: தன் மேல் ஒருசேர வரும் சுமையைத் தாங்கிக்கொண்டு, அரசனுக்குச் செலுத்த வேண்டிய வரியை முழுமையாகச் செலுத்துவதே சிறந்த நாடாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet describes the resilience and wealth of an ideal country. The word 'பொறை' (burden) refers to unexpected pressures, such as an influx of migrants or natural hardships, that fall upon the land all at once ('ஒருங்கு'). A strong nation bears this weight ('தாங்கி') without its economy collapsing. Even while managing such heavy burdens, it remains prosperous enough to pay its taxes ('இறை') in full ('ஒருங்கு') to the ruler ('இறைவற்கு').

ai.literal: Intense hunger and, unceasing disease and, destructive enmity and, without joining, that which functions [is a] country.
ai.translation: A true country is one that functions without being touched by intense hunger, unceasing disease, and destructive enmity.
ai.modern: கொடிய பசியும், தீராத நோயும், அழிக்கும் பகையும் தன்னிடம் சேராமல் நடைபெறும் நாடே சிறந்த நாடாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet defines the ideal state of a nation by listing three major threats it must avoid. Intense hunger points to famine or extreme poverty. Unceasing disease refers to chronic epidemics or poor public health. Destructive enmity indicates external invasions or internal strife. A true country is one that functions and prospers without these three evils ever taking root.

ai.literal: Many factions and, ruin making inner enmity and, king harassing killing rebels and, that which is without is a country.
ai.translation: A true country is one that is free from multiple divided factions, destructive internal enemies, and murderous rebels who harass the sovereign.
ai.modern: பல பிரிவுகளாகப் பிரிந்து கிடக்கும் கூட்டங்களும், நாட்டை அழிக்கும் உட்பகையும், அரசனுக்குத் தொல்லை தரும் கொலைக்குணம் கொண்ட கலகக்காரர்களும் இல்லாததே சிறந்த நாடாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet defines a secure nation by identifying the internal threats it must lack. A good country must be free from multiple divided factions, destructive internal enemies, and violent rebels who constantly trouble the ruling authority. The word 'குறும்பு' refers to rebellious petty chieftains or troublemakers, which perfectly fits the context of harassing the sovereign.

ai.literal: Ruin knowing-not, ruined place-at-even, wealth diminishing-not country, say-they, of countries head.
ai.translation: They say the best of countries is one that knows no ruin, and whose wealth does not diminish even when disaster strikes.
ai.modern: அழிவைச் சந்திக்காததும், ஒருவேளை அழிவு நேர்ந்தாலும் தன் வளம் குறையாததுமான நாடே நாடுகளுள் தலைசிறந்தது என்று கூறுவர்.
ai.explanation: This couplet defines the resilience of an ideal nation. The phrase "கேடு அறியா" means the country naturally avoids destruction. However, the text adds "கெட்ட இடத்தும்" (even when ruined), acknowledging that unforeseen disasters might still strike. In such events, a truly great country is one whose resources ("வளம்") do not diminish ("குன்றா"). The word "தலை" (head) is used metaphorically to mean the chief or the best among all countries.

ai.literal: Two waters and, endowed mountain and, coming water and, strong fortress and, to a country, limbs.
ai.translation: Two sources of water, well-situated mountains, flowing rivers, and strong fortresses are the essential limbs of a country.
ai.modern: மேல்நீர் கீழ்நீர் ஆகிய இருவகை நீர்நிலைகளும், தக்க இடத்தில் அமைந்த மலையும், அதிலிருந்து வரும் ஆற்று நீரும், வலிய கோட்டையும் ஒரு நாட்டிற்கு உறுப்புகளாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet lists the essential physical features that make up a secure and prosperous country. 'Irupuṉal' refers to two types of water sources, typically understood as ground water and surface water. Along with these, well-placed mountains, flowing rivers, and strong fortresses serve as the vital organs or limbs ('uṟuppu') of a nation, providing both sustenance and defense.

ai.literal: Disease-absence, wealth, yield, happiness, security: ornament they-say to-a-country these five.
ai.translation: They say these five are the ornaments of a country: freedom from disease, wealth, rich harvests, happiness, and security.
ai.modern: நோயின்மை, செல்வம், விளைச்சல், மகிழ்ச்சி, பாதுகாப்பு ஆகிய இந்த ஐந்தும் ஒரு நாட்டிற்கு அழகு என்று கூறுவார்கள்.
ai.explanation: This couplet lists the five essential qualities that adorn a prosperous country. 'பிணியின்மை' (absence of disease) ensures a healthy population, while 'செல்வம்' (wealth) and 'விளைவு' (agricultural yield) provide economic stability. 'இன்பம்' (happiness) reflects the well-being of the people, and 'ஏமம்' (security) guarantees their safety. Together, these five elements are described as the true 'அணி' (ornaments) of a nation, making it beautiful and complete.

ai.literal: Country, they say, unseeking wealth-having; countries are not, to seek wealth giving country.
ai.translation: A true country is one that possesses wealth without it having to be sought. A land that yields wealth only through hard seeking is no country at all.
ai.modern: முயன்று தேடாமலேயே செல்வத்தை உடைய நாடே சிறந்த நாடு என்று அறிஞர் கூறுவார்கள். மிகவும் முயன்று தேடிய பிறகே செல்வத்தைத் தரும் நாடு சிறந்த நாடாகாது.
ai.explanation: This couplet defines the ideal economic state of a country. A true country is one where wealth and resources are naturally abundant and easily accessible without strenuous searching. If a land requires its people to struggle and search extensively just to find basic wealth, it does not deserve to be called a great country. The contrast between 'நாடா' (without seeking) and 'நாட' (by seeking) emphasizes that prosperity should be effortless for the inhabitants.

ai.literal: In those ways perfection attained even if, benefit is without indeed, king excellence without country.
ai.translation: Even if a country has achieved all the aforementioned perfections, they are of no use if it lacks an excellent ruler.
ai.modern: மேற்கூறிய எல்லா சிறப்புகளையும் பெற்றிருந்தாலும், சிறந்த அரசன் இல்லாத நாட்டுக்கு அவற்றால் எந்தப் பயனும் இல்லை.
ai.explanation: This couplet concludes the chapter on the features of a good country by emphasizing the paramount importance of leadership. The phrase 'ஆங்கு அமைவு' refers to all the previously mentioned perfections, such as wealth, health, and resources. However, 'பயம் இன்றே' declares that these are completely useless without 'வேந்து அமைவு', which is the excellence of the ruler. The word 'அமைவு' is used twice, contrasting the material perfection of the land with the qualitative perfection of its leadership. Ultimately, a country's natural and acquired greatness depends entirely on the quality of the one who governs it.
